title: Grounding benchmark case
description: One evaluation unit: a claim, the citation(s) attached to it, the evidence pool it was checked against, and the ground-truth label a reviewer assigned. This is the unit the current citation-marker validator and any future entailment verifier are both measured against -- see LABELING.md for how `label` is assigned and README.md for how the runner computes metrics from it.

id.description: Stable identifier, e.g. 'reversed-relationship-003'. Never renumber or reuse once a case has shipped in the sealed split -- that would silently invalidate any previously-recorded sealed-set result.

split.description: dev: free to inspect while iterating on a verifier. calibration: for threshold-tuning only, inspect sparingly. sealed: frozen once labeled; never used to tune prompts, thresholds, or model choice -- only to report a final number.

question.description: The question the claim purports to answer. Optional context, not itself checked.

claim.description: One atomic factual sentence, as a model would produce it in a cited answer.

asserted_citation_ids.description: Citation markers the model attached to `claim`, formatted 'source_id#ordinal' -- the same format tenant_engine.py's _citation_marker() produces. May reference an id/ordinal pair absent from retrieved_evidence, to exercise the invalid-citation path; may be empty, to exercise the no-citation abstention path.

retrieved_evidence.description: The full evidence pool a citation marker is checked against for this case -- i.e. what retrieval actually returned, not just the chunk(s) the claim happens to cite. An empty list represents the no-evidence-retrieved abstention path.

supporting_quotes.description: Exact substrings of some retrieved_evidence[*].content that entail the claim. Required (non-empty) when label == 'supported'; empty for 'contradicted' and 'insufficient'.

label.description: Ground truth: does the cited evidence actually entail the claim? 'contradicted' = cited evidence exists but asserts the opposite or a different fact about the same entities. 'insufficient' = cited evidence doesn't address the claim at all (including: citation invalid/missing, evidence irrelevant, evidence superseded/incomplete).

notes.description: Why this case is in the benchmark -- what specific failure mode it targets. Not used by the runner; for human reviewers and future maintainers.
